title: Anatomy of a CHOP
summary: Official Derivative conceptual article for CHOP internals, covering channels, clips, raw samples, sample rate, start/end intervals, CHOP flags, network cooking, imports/exports, channel expressions, and sample index/value semantics.
guidance: Use this article when a plan needs CHOP data-shape grounding before choosing a specific CHOP operator.
A CHOP holds channels over a shared start-end interval; each channel is an array of raw samples with user-visible names.
If inputs and control parameters are static, a CHOP can be non-time-dependent and will not cook every advancing animation frame.
CHOP channels can drive parameters through exports; exporting is usually preferred over chop() or chopi() expressions when possible.
Export matching is channel-name based, so generated control rigs should plan channel names that match target parameter names.
Channel indexes and values are separate concepts; CHOP samples are index-value pairs and can be evaluated at integer or non-integer indexes.
